items.stem: Why split a game into functions instead of one long block of code?

options.text: Functions organise the code into reusable, named parts that are easier to test and fix
options.rationale: Correct: functions make code reusable, readable and easier to debug.

options.text: Functions make the game run without a computer
options.rationale: Code still needs a computer; functions just organise it.

options.text: Python refuses to run code without functions
options.rationale: Python can run code without functions; they just help.
Functions organise code; they do not play the game.

items.explanation: Correct: functions make code reusable, readable and easier to debug.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO are good reasons to use the random module in a game? (Select TWO.)

options.text: To make the computer's move unpredictable
options.rationale: Correct: randomness stops the computer always doing the same thing.

options.text: To pick a secret number for a guessing game
options.rationale: Correct: random can choose a hidden value.

options.text: To guarantee the player always wins
options.rationale: Randomness does not guarantee a win for anyone.

options.text: To remove the need for a game loop
options.rationale: A game still needs a loop; random does not replace it.

items.explanation: Correct: randomness stops the computer always doing the same thing.

items.stem: A player types 'banana' at a rock/paper/scissors prompt and the game crashes. What is the best fix?

options.text: Validate the input and ask again if it is not a valid choice
options.rationale: Correct: input validation handles unexpected entries safely.

options.text: Tell players never to make mistakes
options.rationale: Programs should handle mistakes, not just forbid them.
The game needs the player's choice.
Crashes should be fixed with validation.

items.explanation: Correct: input validation handles unexpected entries safely.
